Chapter 1: Deciding to Learn Everything and Facing the First Pages
You know that restless feeling you get when life just starts to feel... routine? When every day starts to blur into the next, and your mind’s itching for something—anything—that feels like a real challenge?
For some people, picking up a new hobby does the trick. Maybe it’s running a marathon, or learning to play the guitar. But for one man, that itch led to something a little wild—and honestly, kind of hilarious. He decided he was going to read the entire Encyclopaedia Britannica. Cover to cover. From A all the way to Z.
Now, this wasn’t about showing off. It all started with a mix of simple curiosity, a drive for self-improvement, and yeah—a little insecurity about not knowing enough. Maybe you’ve felt that, too? Like you’re surrounded by people who can toss out fun facts at dinner parties and you wish you had something clever to add. The idea of becoming that person—someone with a story for every topic—was both exciting and, let’s be honest, a little intimidating.
So, he took the first step. It sounds easy, right? Just open up the first volume and start reading. But in reality, facing those dozens of heavy books felt like staring up at a mountain. The first entries—abacuses, aardvarks, you name it—tested his patience right away. The facts were endless, the words packed tight. It was so easy to get lost in the weeds, to wonder if any of this would ever be useful, or if it was just a way to kill time.
At home, this project quickly became impossible to ignore. The books took over shelves and coffee tables. And his partner? Watching with a mix of amusement and concern, not sure if this was just a quirky phase or the start of something much bigger. Friends chimed in too—some with teasing, some with genuine encouragement. There were eye rolls, jokes, but also—if you looked closely—a hint of admiration for even attempting something so bold.
Night after night, reading became a ritual. After work, he’d sit down and tackle a few more pages. Sometimes, the entries were fascinating—stories about lost civilizations, the roots of everyday words, the bizarre lives of animals. Other times, everything just blurred together, and he’d catch himself wondering what he’d gotten himself into. But stubbornness kicked in. He wasn’t about to quit, not yet.
Pretty soon, it was clear this wasn’t just about memorizing trivia. It was about seeing how far determination could really take you. The encyclopedia started to feel like a symbol—a stand-in for all the things that seem just out of reach. Wisdom, confidence, maybe even a little control over the chaos of the world. Most people never try to learn everything, and honestly, that makes sense. But there’s a weird joy in just making the attempt—pushing yourself to see what’s possible.
Those early days were a mix of small wins and frustrating setbacks. Remembering a rare insect felt like conquering Everest, but forgetting a basic date from history? That stung. Still, the project started to change how he saw the world. Suddenly, every conversation, every headline, every random moment became a chance to connect what he’d just read—to spot patterns and hidden links he’d never noticed before.
And here’s the biggest lesson: humility. No matter how much you read, there’s always more. The encyclopedia felt endless—just like the process of learning. The more knowledge he gained, the more he realized how much he didn’t know. It was both thrilling and humbling, a reminder that real intelligence isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about being willing to keep learning, even when the task feels impossible.
